text:
The thorn tree fastens to a rock
its frenzied contortion,
and is the spirit of the wasteland,
twisted with anguish and sun.


The oak is beautiful as Jupiter,
and the flowering myrtle is a Narcissus.
They made this one like Vulcan,
the dreadful forging god.


They made it without the lacy grace
of the bright, trembling poplar,
so the traveler's soul
would never know its pain.


Flowers grow from its shaggy crown.
(So Job's verse was born.)
And like the leper's psalm,
its intense pain is sharp.


Though it fills the blazing air
of midday with its scent,
its dark tangled crown has never felt
a nest tremble within it…


It told me that it knows me,
that on a night of pain,
in its dense million thorns,
my heart was bruised.


I embraced it like a sister,
as if Hagar embraced Job,
in a clasp that is not tenderness,
but something more: despair!

translation.title: The Thorn Tree
